title: Trajectory forecasting lifts the femtosecond ceiling in molecular simulation - Nature Machine Intelligence
gist: This record is a subscription-gated preview stub: beyond a one-line summary that a new deep learning method enables molecular dynamics simulations over longer time scales while preserving accurate physical property prediction, the retrieved text is subscription pricing, a figure caption and a reference list. Note the discrepancy — the raw metadata marks the record as not paywalled, yet the body states it is a preview of subscription content; the commentary is by Seyed Mohamad Moosavi of the University of Toronto and the Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence.

insights.claim: A new deep learning method reportedly allows molecular dynamics simulations to run over longer time scales while still producing accurate physical property predictions, attacking the timestep limitation that constrains conventional simulation.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Longer accessible simulation time scales at fixed compute would expand what materials and drug discovery workflows can model without more hardware.
insights.quote: A new deep learning method enables molecular dynamics simulations over longer time scales while still achieving accurate physical property prediction.

insights.claim: The framing shift described is from explicit time integration to trajectory forecasting in molecular dynamics — replacing step-by-step numerical integration with learned prediction of where the system goes next.
insights.speaker: Nature Machine Intelligence
insights.so_what: Substituting learned forecasting for numerical integration is the same pattern already reshaping weather modeling; watch it spread to other simulation-heavy sectors.
insights.quote: From explicit time integration to trajectory forecasting in MD.
